title: Open centre, no isolani: the d-file with both queens still on it

difficulty.label: Black in the Ruy Lopez Exchange after the centre opens

objective.summary: No isolani on either side and one fully pawnless central file: neither colour has a pawn on the d-file, and both queens are still on the board — which is exactly what the shape library's open-centre entry requires before it fires. This drill asks for the state the entry's Black plan names: both queens off the board with a central file still open. The corpus's most-played continuation reaches it on Black's third move, and the entry's own trigger stops firing at that moment, because it requires the queens to be present.

planClasses.label: Trade the queens with the file still open
planClasses.description: The library's Black plan for this entry. Its success signature is a state change this pack can check and does: both queens off the board while a central file is still open. Evaluated on the authored positions, it is false at the start and at the moment Black's queen lands on d1, and true from White's recapture onwards.

planClasses.label: Put a knight on a central square
planClasses.description: The library's other Black plan for this entry. Its success signature is stricter than arrival — a black knight on d4 or e4 that the detector also reads as an outpost. Measured on this spine: Black's king's knight stands on g8 in all ten authored positions and no black knight reaches d4 or e4 in any of them, so this pack's spine never tests the signature.

annotations: Read the structure first. White pawns: a2, b2, c2, e4, f2, g2, h2. Black pawns: a6, b7, c6, c7, f6, g7, h7. Neither side has a pawn on the d-file, so the d-file is open in the detector's sense; White's pawn on e4 means the e-file is not. Both queens are on the board. Those are the conditions the shape library's open-centre entry requires, and its trigger fires here.

Computed from this position: d4 is occupied by a White knight and attacked once by each side (White queen d1, Black queen d8); the black king's knight is still on g8. Black's two c-pawns are the doubled pair the capture on move three produced, and one of them is about to move.

Lichess explorer, rapid+classical, rating bands 1400/1600/1800, 2023-01 to 2025-12: this position occurs in 2634 games, the largest node in this content wave. c5 is the most-played move at 1221 (46.4%), then Bc5 865 (32.8%), Bd6 243 (9.2%), Ne7 135 (5.1%), Bd7 69 (2.6%). Every move on this spine is the most-played move at its node at this band.

1219 games here, and the top four replies are within four percentage points of each other: Nb3 327 (26.8%), Nf3 307 (25.2%), Ne2 285 (23.4%), Nf5 281 (23.1%), then Qh5+ 13 (1.1%). The selection rule picks Nb3 by a margin of twenty games out of twelve hundred, which is the thinnest 'most played' on any spine in this wave — the counts are stated so you can treat all four as live.

326 games; Qxd1 is the most played at 269 (82.5%), then Be6 32 (9.8%), Bd6 13 (4.0%), c4 4 (1.2%), b6 4 (1.2%). This is the move the objective is written around, and the corpus plays it four times in five.

Evaluated on the position after this move, the plan signature this pack grades is still false: Black's queen is on d1 but has not been captured, so both queens are still on the board. It becomes true one ply later.

269 games, and Rxd1 is played in all 269 (100%) — the only reply the band contains. Evaluated here: the shape entry's Black plan signature now holds (no queen of either colour, the d-file still open), and the entry's own trigger stops firing, because it requires both queens to be present. Those two facts are the same fact seen from two expressions.

Computed on this position: the d-file is still pawnless, d8 is attacked once by White (rook d1) and once by Black (king e8), and d4 is attacked twice by White (rook d1, knight b3) and once by Black (pawn c5).

269 games; Be6 is the most played at 80 (29.7%), then Bd6 70 (26.0%), Bd7 50 (18.6%), Bg4 44 (16.4%), b6 16 (5.9%). Four bishop moves inside thirteen percentage points of each other — this is a node where the corpus has no consensus and the compare view has four real doors.
80 games; Bf4 is the most played at 58 (72.5%), then Nc3 9 (11.3%), Be3 8 (10.0%), N1d2 2 (2.5%), Na5 1 (1.3%).

58 games; c4 is the most played at 39 (67.2%), then Rc8 7 (12.1%), c6 4 (6.9%), Bxb3 3 (5.2%), Bd6 2 (3.4%). The pawn steps off the square from which it was the only black attacker of d4 — recomputed after White's reply, d4 is attacked once by White (rook d1) and zero times by Black.
The d-file is still pawnless after this move, so the structure this pack detects is unchanged.

39 games; Nd4 is the most played at 24 (61.5%), then Na5 14 (35.9%), Rd8+ 1 (2.6%). A White knight occupies the central square on the open file; Black's king's knight is still on g8, as it is in every authored position of this pack. Evaluated on this position, Tabiya's outpost detector does not read d4 as a White outpost — the square is occupied, not owned, by the same standard the entry's plan signature applies to Black.
This is where the band's data thins to a few dozen games. Past here you are playing it out rather than reading it, which is the point of the drill.

The second-most-played reply at 70 of 269 (26.0%), within ten games of Be6. The bishop goes to the open file instead of the diagonal. The resulting position is reached by 70 games in this band, where White plays Be3 27 (38.6%), Na5 19 (27.1%), Nc3 15 (21.4%), c4 3 (4.3%), c3 2 (2.9%). The plan signature this pack grades holds on this branch too — both queens are already off — so the two branches differ in piece placement, not in the state the objective checks.

checkpoints.label: Before your first move: which of the library's two Black plans are you playing?
Both queens are off and the d-file is still pawnless
The c-pawn steps forward and d4 loses its only black attacker
No queens, d-file open — the state this pack's objective checks

deviations.note: Bc5: 865 of 2634 (32.8%), the second-most-played move in the start position at this band and only thirteen points behind the spine move. The resulting position is reached by 865 games where White plays c3 206 (23.8%), Be3 196 (22.7%), Qh5+ 183 (21.2%), Nf5 107 (12.4%), Nb3 89 (10.3%). It leaves the c6 pawn where it is, so the doubled pair stays doubled — a fact about the skeleton, not a comparison.
Bd6: 243 of 2634 (9.2%), the third-most-played move here.

Ne7: 135 of 2634 (5.1%). It is the only move in this node's top five that moves the king's knight, and that knight stands on g8 in all ten authored positions of this pack. The shape entry's Black outpost plan needs a black knight on d4 or e4, so this is the only measured door in the corpus toward the plan class this spine never tests.
Bd7: 69 of 2634 (2.6%), the fifth-most-played move in the band's table for this position.

Bg4: 44 of 269 (16.4%) at this node, the fourth of four bishop moves the corpus spreads itself across. The objective's state is already satisfied before this move, so nothing in this pack's grading distinguishes it from the spine move.

Bxb3: 3 of 58 (5.2%) at this node. The corpus contains three examples in three years of this band, which is the whole evidence base for it; it is listed so the compare view has a door, not because anything measured it.

feedbackClaims.text: The band's own results at this position are on record and are stated here as a fact about what happened. Over 2634 games (Lichess explorer, ratings 1400/1600/1800, speeds rapid+classical, 2023-01 to 2025-12, retrieved 2026-08-15) the outcomes were 1309 white wins, 197 draws and 1128 black wins (49.7/7.5/42.8%). Stated as what happened, per the owner ruling of 2026-08-15: a result split may be stated with its population and may never be converted into a move verdict or a quality claim. No move, plan or side in this pack is graded from these numbers.

At the Lichess 1400/1600/1800 bands (rapid and classical, 2023-01 to 2025-12) the start position occurs in 2634 games. Two of the spine's eight moves dominate their node — Qxd1 269 of 326 (82.5%) and Rxd1 269 of 269 (100%) — and two do not: at 1219 games the top four replies sit within four points of each other, and at 269 games four bishop moves sit within thirteen.

The shape entry's trigger and its Black plan signature were both evaluated on every authored position of this pack. The trigger fires on the first three and stops at the fourth; the plan signature is false on the first three and true from the fourth onward. The crossing point is the queen recapture, because the trigger requires both queens present and the plan requires both queens gone. That is a property of the two expressions, not a claim about the position.

Black's king's knight stands on g8 in all ten authored positions of this pack, and no black knight occupies d4 or e4 in any of them. The entry's Black outpost plan is therefore named but never tested by this spine; the one measured corpus move toward it is ...Ne7 at 135 of 2634 (5.1%) in the start position.

Every split below was re-queried live for this pass rather than copied from a document, and every position total reproduced the count this pack already quoted. Result splits are admissible corpus_observed evidence under the owner ruling of 2026-08-15 (design/BACKLOG.md D126); the boundary is that a split may be stated with its population and may never be converted into a move verdict or a quality claim. Measured here: start position 2634 games, 1309 white / 197 draw / 1128 black (49.7/7.5/42.8%). No verdict, preference, comparison or cost is derived from any of these numbers anywhere in this pack. The repo's own explorer client abstains below 100 games at a position (apps/server/src/sourcing/explorer.ts), and that floor is applied here: where a position falls under it the split is recorded as unavailable rather than quoted.

SPINE SELECTION RULE (mechanical): every spine move is the most-played move at that node at this band, with no ties to break. Where the margin is small the counts are stated at the node rather than smoothed over. The sibling branch ...Bd6 is the second-most-played reply at its node.

STRUCTURAL READINGS (mechanical, chessops): the pawn skeletons, the attacker counts for d1, d4 and d8 at each quoted position, the occupancy of g8 across all ten authored positions, the absence of any pawn on the d-file, and the outpost detector's reading of d4 for White at the last spine node were computed from the FENs in this file with the chessops attack tables, not recalled.

SHAPE REFERENCE (mechanical): the open-centre entry's trigger was evaluated on every authored position of this pack; it fires on the first three and stops after the queens are exchanged, which is the clause of its own trigger requiring at least one queen of each colour. The entry's Black plan signature (both queens off with a central file still open) was evaluated on the same set and holds from the queen recapture onward, which is why this pack's objective can consume it as a plan consequence. The plan classes reference the entry's own plans rather than restating them; the entry's plan prose carries its own UNGROUNDED provenance and this pack does not improve it.

UNGROUNDED: the objective summary's framing — that reaching the queenless position with the file still open is what this position is about for Black — is this pack's one authored strategic premise. It rests on the shape entry naming that plan for this side, and the entry's own prose is uncited. The corpus shows what the band plays, not what is correct. No engine evaluation has been run on any position in this pack.

NOT CLAIMED: no move in this pack is graded better or worse than another, no plan is asserted to be best, and no deviation note asserts a chess consequence beyond an explicitly measured one. In particular, nothing here claims that the queen trade favours Black, that the doubled c-pawns are a weakness or a strength, or that Black's knight belongs on any square.

CITATION PASS (2026-08-16): en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruy_Lopez,_Exchange_Variation (CC BY-SA 4.0, read 2026-08-16) states this pack's objective premise directly — "White aims to reach an endgame with a superior pawn structure, which may become an important factor" — notes that "Black has gained the bishop pair at the cost of a weakened pawn structure, having doubled pawns on c6 and c7", and gives the endgame plan as "to create a passed pawn on the kingside, while Black is unable to do the same on the queenside because of the doubled pawns". WHAT IT DOES NOT SUPPLY: the source frames the target as an endgame; this pack's objective is a queenless MIDDLEGAME with the open file, which is a narrower and different state, and no consulted source names it. Pack prose is CC-BY-SA-4.0; attribution is encoded in provenance.attribution.

graduationBlockers.statement: CITED 2026-08-16 (the trade-into-a-better-structure premise). That White plays this variation to reach a favourable endgame off Black's doubled c-pawns is stated by en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruy_Lopez,_Exchange_Variation (CC BY-SA 4.0), attributed in provenance.attribution.

STILL UNCITED after the 2026-08-16 pass: the cited source's target is an ENDGAME with a healthy kingside majority; this pack's objective is the queenless middlegame with the open file, which the source does not name as a goal. The inherited UNGROUNDED provenance of the open-centre entry is untouched, and no corpus measurement relating the queen trade to results at this band has been done.
No engine pass has been run on this pack. No deviation carries a cost for that reason.

This pack declares no timing window. The measured reason: the only candidate race is Black's queen trade against White's occupation of the open file, and the corpus shows the recapture is forced (269 of 269), so there is no opponent lever whose arrival ends a preparation. A window here would be an invention.

The shape entry this pack references fires on only three of its ten authored positions, because the entry's trigger requires both queens. Whether an entry that stops describing the position after three plies is the right library hook for this tabiya is an open question this pack surfaces and does not settle.
